title: Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker
subtitle: A tiny world worth turning around
summary: Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker is Nintendo's miniature puzzle adventure, first released for Wii U in Japan on 13 November 2014.
body: Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker is Nintendo's miniature puzzle adventure, first released for Wii U in Japan on 13 November 2014. Captain Toad and Toadette cross compact diorama-like levels, looking for treasure and rescuing one another from Wingo. Their heavy backpacks keep them from jumping, making the shape of the route especially important. A ledge that looks unreachable from one side may connect to a hidden passage behind it, so rotating the view becomes a practical part of finding the way through each small world.

The Wii U GamePad lets the player turn the camera and interact with the scene. That change of viewpoint reveals paths, enemies and items concealed by the level's own structure. Walking, climbing and plucking objects provide the main tools, while optional collectibles and challenges give another reason to inspect a completed stage. The limited movement makes the environment carry the puzzle: the player studies where a path begins, what blocks it and which viewpoint exposes the connection to the destination.

The idea grew from Captain Toad's stages in Super Mario 3D World. Directors Kenta Motokura and Shinya Hiratake developed it into a complete game, with music by Naoto Kubo and Mahito Yokota. The backpack supplies a character-based explanation for the restriction that defines the design. Switch and Nintendo 3DS editions followed in 2018 with additional content. The original Wii U release turns a familiar platform world into something to examine from all sides, making careful looking as rewarding as the movement of its small explorer.
